status: bounded exploratory extension after reading the previous network/pathway report
prior_results: Earlier aggregate national groupings, city entry ordering, community participation and gateway mixing were already tested; do not present them as new tests or hide their weak adjusted results.
literature_questions: Does country-level recruitment describe the subsequent trajectory of the same researchers?
Do domestic onward moves broaden the arrival distribution while preserving a hierarchical selection of destinations?

sample: existing76 countries, first recorded confirmed international entry into each destination country in2012-2018; no nationality or permanent residence claims
primary_extension_1: Split the next international move into return to the immediately preceding origin country vs onward move to a third country. Retain domestic next move, no recorded intercity change, and unresolved next move as separate categories.
primary_extension_2: For domestic redistributors, classify destinations by whether they were established during1998-2011 and compare log early domestic city-strength changes with same-origin/same-move-year ordinary domestic flows.
replications: observed next-transition gap restricted to1 or2 years
alternative country minimum cohort counts100 and500
inference: country as analysis unit for cross-country comparisons; adjusted benchmark contrasts, country bootstrap and exact country sign tests; Holm across paired pre-defined benchmark metrics; descriptive route proportions not causal effects
classification: Do not force number of country types. First inspect directly interpretable route profiles and their sensitivity. Relative path proportions are behavioral profiles, not discovered natural types.
limitations: Microdata are a strict unambiguous geographic-match subset of canonical events
